notes: Eval 0 (notification dup-check) doesn't discriminate: both configs investigate the repo thoroughly and land on the same composition-first conclusion. Not a flaw in the skill - just means this eval alone wouldn't justify it.

Eval 2 (MSN drift) is the clearest differentiator: without the skill, the model defaults to prescribing unilateral action on a cross-cutting governance/process change; with the skill, it explicitly separates the contained code fix (does it) from the process change (escalates to Captain/Chief of Staff per its own Escalation section). This is the skill's real value-add, not just formatting.

Eval 1 (advisory-workbench review): with-skill run uses the Standard Response Format correctly, but the baseline run actually surfaced a sharper, more specific bug (18-officer vs 5-person specialist registry mismatch on the new default 'Ask' view) that the with-skill run didn't find - it focused more on test-coverage gaps instead. Worth watching in future iterations whether structure/escalation focus trades off against investigation depth on any single finding.

With-skill runs took ~40% longer on average (205.9s vs 146.7s) and used slightly more tokens - expected cost of following the fuller persona/format, not a red flag on its own given the pass-rate gain.
